module_title: State Executive: Governor and Chief Minister - Basic Understanding
introduction: Part VI of the Constitution (Articles 153 to 167) deals with the State Executive. The state executive consists of the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the state. Similar to the Centre, the state has a parliamentary system where the Governor is the nominal head and the Chief Minister is the real head.

core_concepts.title: The Governor (Article 153)
core_concepts.description: The Constitution states that there shall be a Governor for each state. The Governor is the 'Constitutional Head' (Nominal Executive). All executive actions are taken in their name. Under the 7th Amendment Act (1956), the same person can be appointed as Governor for two or more states.

core_concepts.title: The Chief Minister (Article 164)
core_concepts.description: The Chief Minister is the 'Real Executive' (Head of the Government) at the state level. The Governor appoints the leader of the majority party in the State Legislative Assembly as the Chief Minister.

core_concepts.title: Appointment and Tenure
core_concepts.description: The Governor is appointed by the 'President of India' and holds office during the 'pleasure of the President' (normal term is 5 years). The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.

core_concepts.title: Qualifications
core_concepts.description: To become a Governor, one must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age. To become a Chief Minister (as an MLA), the minimum age requirement is 25 years.

important_entities.name: Sarojini Naidu
important_entities.significance: She became the Governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) and famously described the position of the Governor as 'a bird in a golden cage'.

important_entities.name: Sucheta Kripalani
important_entities.key_fact: First Female Chief Minister of India
important_entities.significance: She served as the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, breaking significant political ground for women in India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume the Governor is indirectly elected. Remember, there is NO election (direct or indirect) for the Governor in India; they are directly 'nominated/appointed' by the Central Government (President).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 35 for the State Head, 25 for the State Lead
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Governor = Minimum 35 years. Chief Minister (if from the lower house) = Minimum 25 years.

exam_strategy_tips: Article 153 (Governors of States) and Article 164 (Appointment of CM and Ministers) are highly frequently asked in basic objective exams.
Which amendment allowed one person to be the Governor of multiple states? (Answer: 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956).
